newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Ecuador oil min says pipeline deal near.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ecuador oil min says pipeline deal near.

text.p: After years of false starts, the Ecuadoran government is close to wrapping up a $120 million plan to expand the strategic Transecuadoran crude oil pipeline system (SOTE), Energy and Mines Minister Ral Baca Carbo said here on Monday.
Baca also said that two recently expired export contracts for a total 36,000 barrels a day of crude oil would be awarded soon.

The private companies which are expected to finance the expansion are U.S. oil major Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO), City Investing of Canada, Argentina's YPF, Los Angeles-based Occidental Petroleum Corp and Oryx Energy of Dallas.
The companies would recover their costs through an increase in the pipeline tariff, and the timing of the companies' cost recovery is currently being negotiated, Baca said.
"As a function of the tariff increase, and as a function of the increase in production, (we are negotiating) what will be the timing for amortization," Baca said.
A final meeting with the companies is scheduled for June 15, he said.
About 50,000 bpd of production which is currently shut in due to the lack of pipeline capacity would initially come on stream once the expansion is complete next year, he said.
The existing SOTE pipeline, which runs from Lago Agrio in the eastern oil-producing region to the Pacific port of Balao, is used to transport around 85 percent of Ecuador's 390,000 bpd oil output.
The expansion project is fairly simple from an engineering perspective, involving the replacement of some tubing, installation of new pumps and an increase in storage and loading capacity.

The upgrade, however, had long been held up because of political disputes. An expansion of the pipeline had been agreed last year by the Bacaram government, which fell in February. But that deal fell apart because of accusations of corruption and disputes about how the contracted companies would be compensated.

Baca added that the 90,000 bpd of new transport capacity would go toward private-sector flows, not just from current fields but also from a planned tender for eight marginal oil fields and several enhanced recovery operations for existing fields such as Shushufindi.
Ecuador currently exports about 240,000 bpd of "Oriente" crude, most of which goes to the U.S. Gulf Coast. Oil exports account for the bulk of Ecuador's foreign earnings.

On the award of the expired contracts, Baca said a tender for the first contract for 24,000 bpd, previously held by Mexico's state-owned Pemex International, would begin this month. The other is for 12,000 bpd, which was with Totisa, a subsidiary of local trader Tripetrol.
He stressed that transparency was the government's first priority in awarding contracts. "The transparency that we want translates into tenders to authorize from now on any type of concession."
